chunks: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Ibn Muskan, from Ubayd Allah al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام about salat al-kusuf: should we make it up if it passes us by? He said: “There is no qada' for it.” Yet it had been held by us that it is to be made up. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: the proper way regarding these reports is that we understand the falling away of qada' to apply when the disk has not been completely eclipsed; but if it has been completely eclipsed, then qada' is unavoidable. This is indicated by that.

key_terms.سُقُوطَ الْقَضَاءِ: the dropping of the obligation of make-up prayer
key_terms.فَاتَتْنَا: when it has been missed by us
key_terms.قَضَاءٌ: making up a missed ritual prayer

ai.seo_question: Is qada' required for a missed salat al-kusuf in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal ruling of making up salat al-kusuf when it has been missed. The apparent negation of qada' is reconciled by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan as applying to a partial eclipse, while a total eclipse requires qada'.
